title: The Pile-Up
logline: An evening's worth of trouble lands on one white page behind a small painted bot asleep on his clay bar; he wakes, watches it heap up, strikes the words out, climbs over his bar (the app's own launch move, bar and all) and sorts it one card at a time: a filler word flicked off a spoken sentence, a note hung on 5 pm the way he hangs himself, scraps swept into one trip, a hand that stops short of the button, a question he waits on with the beat gone. His team pops up under him and takes a note from his hand, he paints his bar back, swings home onto it, paints his mark and winks.

Never two colours in one frame except the team row (the four dotted heads, once) and the end card (clay only). Cream #FBF2E2 is the bot's eyes and gloves only: the beetle has no eyes, the tape is grey, the sparkle is sea. Moss is ONE constant #4F7A3A in every moss pixel: head-code.png and swash-moss.png are exactly that already; underline-2f5d50.png (#2F5D50, the brief's old moss) is never drawn; underline-4f7a3a is regenerated. beats.psychology: PATTERN INTERRUPT: a flat, white, hand-painted frame with one breathing shape in a feed of moving photographic video reads as 'not an ad' and stops the thumb. EYES AND FACES: two big cream eyes snapping open at 0.33 s is the strongest attention trigger there is, and an upside-down face makes the brain work half a second longer to resolve it. MOTION ONSET at 1.0 s (the first thing falls) re-hooks anyone about to scroll; his eyes following it make the viewer's eyes follow too (joint attention), which is why the pieces fall BEHIND him: the eyes are never covered. CURIOSITY GAP: what is this creature, and what is falling on it?

beats.visual: Things keep landing bottom-right in the column x 600-1070 and heap up on the chat card, all WORDLESS, ink, grey and white: f80 a blank grey torn scrap (#ECE9E3, 380x220), f96 a blank ticket card (white, 420x200, a dashed ink perforation, no words), f104 the ink sun with a small cloud, f112 a blank scrap (#D9D5CD), f116 a blank stay card (white, 420x120), f120 the blank packing scrap (seed 92, #FBF8F2), f124 a blank scrap (#FBFAF7), f128 the ring card (white, 480x270) with the wide loose ink ring across its middle and an eyeless ink beetle sitting on the ring's top-right. The pile is felt, not read: the only words on the page are Mom's and the note's, already read at camera 1.0, and the headline. Every card and scrap carries the same graphite shadow (hatch at one scale, clipped, offset +6, +9): one light. The heap's top is near y 920 (world) by f128 and its upper tiers stay right of x 600 so the headline keeps clean paper. The headline writes bottom-left: 'It all' / 'piles up'. All of it falls and heaps BEHIND him.

beats.psychology: RELATABILITY: one true everyday moment, the evening when everything lands at once; the viewer sees their own pile. EMOTIONAL ARC, TENSION: accelerating drops, a riser, widening eyes, a grip tightening on the bar. RHYTHM AND ENTRAINMENT: a calm 56 bpm heartbeat under a 112.5 pulse and rising mess, so the body feels 'too much' before the mind reads it. PROCESSING FLUENCY: four short words and a wordless heap, so nothing competes with them. CONTRAST AND NEGATIVE SPACE: the left column above the headline and the whole top stay empty; blank grey scraps make the heap mass rather than text.

beats.psychology: DIRECT GAZE: a face that has found you holds social attention; we cannot easily look away from eyes that look back. THE COMIC HOLD: a full beat of stillness before action is where the character lives (react, hold, decide). ZEIGARNIK OPEN LOOP: striking the words out announces a decision without saying what it is, so the viewer has to stay to see. The strike is motivated, handmade and a little funny: it marks the turn from tension to action.

beats.name: Up and over, the bar goes too, then a peek
beats.visual: Same frame. He pulls himself up over the bar and is gone, and then the app's own launch move plays out in full with nobody in frame: the bar springs, his two gloves come back over it, pinch it and pull it in to its middle until it is gone. White paper and the heap. One frame later two cream gloves grip the top edge of the heap's top card (the ring card) and his head rises behind it the right way up, as bot-curious, peeking over the problem itself. He glances up at the empty paper where his bar was, then at you.

beats.psychology: ANTICIPATION BY WITHHOLDING: he vanishes and the stage has no face for 1.3 s; the brain leans in to fill the gap, and what fills it is the brand's own launch animation (the gloves come back and pull the bar in), so the viewer has met the app's opening move before they have met the app. MERE EXPOSURE: the same silhouette returns in a new place and orientation, and recognising it is its own small pleasure. HUMOUR: the whack-a-mole pop from behind the very thing that was piling up. The glance at the empty paper is a tiny character beat that says he chose this. CONTINUITY: no bar is left behind and none is carried; the only bar that persists is the one he paints at the end.

beats.psychology: VOICE MADE VISIBLE: 'Say it' on the cut and three pulsing listen dots at the speech's origin tell a muted viewer this is spoken, not typed, before a single word appears. HUMOUR THROUGH A PHYSICAL GAG: the filler word is literally flicked off the page, so 'filler out, punctuation in' becomes slapstick the viewer feels rather than reads. PREDICTION ERROR: the viewer's brain fills the hole where 'late' should be a frame before 'late' slides in late; being right is rewarded, and the gag restates the sentence. RELATABILITY: a real family chat, in the language people actually speak, and a true everyday message everyone has sent. CONTRAST: grey wobbling handwriting beside crisp black type is the before and after in one frame. PROCESSING FLUENCY: one idea per shot, messy in, clean out.

beats.name: Keybot: sent, and the first colour
beats.visual: Same layout. The message is sent and rises into the chat as a black bubble (the chat scrolls up 70 px, Mom's bubble clipping at the card top as a real chat does). beats.psychology: ANTICIPATION: a dot that holds a beat while the drone breathes out, so the return is anticipated rather than announced and the page never reads as 'the video ended'. MERE EXPOSURE AND RECOGNITION: the exact icon the viewer will meet in the store appears at the moment of maximum goodwill, built back in front of them: bar, gloves, bot. EMOTIONAL RESOLUTION: the hero goes home to his bar; eyes shut through the fall and opening on you afterwards makes the eye contact its own beat. COMPLETION ON THE LOUDEST BEAT: the brain was watching a shape being drawn; the ring closing as the boom lands is a stronger button than a slam, and the mark is the brand's own hand. components.name: sound extensions (sound.mjs)
components.source_or_how: Two new kinds: paper-thud = noise(0.08 s, alpha 0.08, a 0.002, tau 0.03) + tone(70, 0.1, 0.002, 0.03) + tone(190, 0.05, 0.001, 0.02) at gain 0.5 (a soft paper landing with a knock a phone can hear); boing = tone(180, 0.25, 0.003, 0.08, glide 1.45) (the bar springing). PHONE BODIES on the existing low kinds: pulse = its 70 Hz thump + a woody knock tone(220, 0.06, 0.001, 0.02, glide 0.82) + a noise transient (0.02 s, alpha 0.3) at -4 dB; heart = its 58/52 Hz pair + tone(150, 0.12) and tone(140, 0.1) at -6 dB; boom = its f0 -> f1 sub + a body tone(110, 0.5-0.6, glide 0.82) + a noise front (0.04 s, alpha 0.15) 3 dB louder than before; drone = 55 Hz + partials at 165 Hz (-14 dB) and 220 Hz (-18 dB). The bot bells are the existing 'bell' kind at D4 293.66, F#4 369.99, A4 440, B4 493.88, hero D5 587.33, 'yours' E5 659.25. MIX PASS: audition the whole render through a 300 Hz high-pass (the phone-speaker proxy) and confirm the beat, the half-time structure, the hole at f736-f816 and the two booms all read; master to -14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP; then play it muted and loud on a real 390 px phone before locking any gag that depends on the beat. No voice in v1 (a TTS 'sample' line ducked -6 dB remains possible later; the film must read with it off).

sound_design: Everything is the brand's own synth (sound.mjs), no licensed music, no voice, and every low cue now has a body above 130 Hz so the rhythm exists on a phone speaker, with the sub kept for headphones; the mix is auditioned through a 300 Hz high-pass and mastered to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP. THE BED: no bed for the first 2.1 s (the hook is pure picture); one soft paper rustle on the eye snap at f10 so sound-on viewers know the audio is alive; two near-silent paper thuds at f48 and f64; a 55 Hz drone with quiet 165/220 Hz partials fades in at f64 and holds under the whole middle, fading out f952-f984 so its last breath runs under the clay dot. THE BEAT: 112.5 BPM, BEAT = 16 frames at 30 fps, so every 8th (8 f) and 16th (4 f) is a whole frame and every cut, pop, underline and bell lands on the grid the WAV is cut to. The pulse (a 70 Hz thump with a woody 220 -> 180 Hz knock and a noise click) is FULL-TIME only where the picture is dense: f64-f112 (under the accelerando of paper thuds, gains 0.3 -> 0.7, with a 56 bpm heartbeat and a riser ending on the ring card's landing and a boom at f128) and f864-f944 (the team arriving, two per beat on the 8ths). Under the four episodes it is HALF-TIME (one thump per two beats, f256 to f736) so soft paper sounds breathe; the 8th-note texture comes from the action itself (keys per landed word with one HOLE at f324 where 'late' should be, 'land' ticks per stacked scrap, swing-end ticks on the pendulum). KEY MOMENTS: the launch whoosh and the boing of the bar (f180, f190), then the gloves coming back, the pinch click and the suck whoosh with only the drone and the heartbeat under the faceless stage (f205-f227); the flick whoosh twice (f304, f768, a callback the ear predicts); the 'land' of the note hooking the rail (f464); the brand's 'stop' two-note as the hand stops short, on the beat (f640); and THE HOLE: from f736 the pulse is absent for five beats under 'Go live?', the heartbeat alone at f784 and f816, the tap at f816 bringing the pulse back. THE CHORD STRUCTURE: each bot has one note, struck the moment its colour arrives on its underline: Keybot D4 (f384), Plan F#4 (f560), Travel A4 (f672), Code bot B4 (f840): the chord is one note short all film. In the team row the four notes return one per head (f872-f896) with a single higher E5 ping for 'yours' (f904), and at f936, with the clay underline, the full chord rings for the first time (D4 F#4 A4 B4 and the hero's D5 over a D3 pad). THE RETURN: a tick for the dot over the drone's tail (f976), eight silent frames, the brush 'shhk' of the bar painting itself (f992); two glove slaps (f1016, f1020); a soft boom as he settles (f1048); the listen bell as his eyes open (f1056); 'write' and 'land' for the two slashes; a rising whoosh round the 0; and THE STING at f1088: the big boom (sub 62 -> 36 under a 110 -> 90 Hz body and a hard noise front, gain 0.8) exactly as the 0 closes, with the final chord (D3 pad plus the five bells, dur 2.5-3.0). Then only small sounds (the write of the line, the stamp's press, a blink click) and the wink's short D5 bell at f1152; everything has decayed by f1167 and the last 16 frames are silent, so the loop back to the sleeping bot is a quiet cut.
why_it_works: It is a story, not a feature list, and the story has one shape the brain already loves: a small creature faces too much, handles it with charm one piece at a time, and goes home. Every product truth is carried by an action rather than a claim (a filler word flicked off a spoken sentence, a word that arrives late, a note hung on 5 pm by a bot who hangs upside down himself, scraps swept into one card as handwriting becomes type, a hand that stops short of 'Open to book', a question he waits on with the beat gone, a note handed to the right bot), so the viewer infers what the app does the way they infer character in a Pixar short: by watching hands and eyes. The hook works mute because it is pure picture: a still, breathing, hand-painted white frame in a feed of moving footage, two big eyes snapping open upside down at a third of a second, something falling at one second with the eyes following it, and nothing ever crossing those eyes because the pile builds behind him. From there the structure is a steady 112.5 bpm cut to whole frames, with one colour per episode on a white page, so each shot is one idea read in a glance on a phone; every readable word sits inside the Reels, Shorts and TikTok safe box and above 1250, and the pulse that carries the rhythm has a body a phone speaker can reproduce, so the one place it drops out, the 'Go live?' wait, is a physical event rather than a missing texture. The critique's fixes make the spine stronger without bloating it: the launch move plays in full twice (the gloves come back and pull the bar in), so the icon's animation becomes a character habit instead of a continuity error; 'Say it' and three listen dots make the voice visible; the heap is wordless so the headline owns the frame; the code fix is one anyone can see is a fix; moss is one colour on two things that say the same sentence; the breath before the yes is visible; the brush marks are never squashed; the hero returns at the exact size and place he left, so the loop is true; and the whole film boils like paint. The opening pile is a Zeigarnik loop the viewer watches shut item by item (the heap below the stage card goes 3, 2, 1, 0), the copy is plain and true to the build with every word at 44 px or more, and the last three seconds are the best three: the boom and chord resolving, the name, the url in a hand-drawn stamp, eye contact, a wink, then stillness and silence that loop straight back into the sleeping bot at frame 0.
build_notes:
GRID. The timeline is authored in FRAMES. BPM 112.5 so that BEAT = 16 f at 30 fps, 8th = 8 f, 16th = 4 f; t = f / 30. Beat anchors (beat -> frame -> s): b0 f0 0.000 | b4 f64 2.133 | b8 f128 4.267 | b11 f176 5.867 | b16 f256 8.533 | b23 f368 12.267 | b26 f416 13.867 | b36 f576 19.200 | b44 f704 23.467 | b49 f784 26.133 | b54 f864 28.800 | b61 f976 32.533 | b68 f1088 36.267 | b74 f1184 39.467 (end). Every event above is a frame number; window.__cues() is generated from the same frame table (at = f / 30), so the picture and the WAV cannot drift. Duration 74 beats = 1184 f = 39.467 s. Write trailer.html's timeline as beat and 16th indices against const BEAT_F = 16 so the grid is one number; intra-beat choreography (arcs, flips, squashes) is in frames and stays.

CANVAS AND UNITS. 1080x1920 primary, 1920x1080 secondary, both from one timeline; sizes in u (one px at the 1080 short side) as engine.js already does; `portrait` switches the composition where the two differ (every beat lists both). Deterministic: everything is a pure function of f; seeded rng for jitter, specks, scrawl, boil index.

LAYER ORDER (back to front), every frame: 1 #FFFFFF fill; 2 paper.png cover at 0.9; 3 camera transform (only f64-f176: 1.00 -> 0.85 about (540, 560), E.io, then held; hard cut to 1.0 at f256); 4 the stage card(s) with hatch shadows under them; 5 the heap / scraps / tray items / the falling pieces (each with its hatch shadow, offset +6, +9, one light): in 9:16 the opening pieces fall and heap HERE, behind the bot, so no drop crosses an eye; 6 the bot: hang() (head behind the bar, bar, gloves) or peek() (face, then glove sprites); 7 flying objects that must pass in front of him: the 'umm' scrap, the beetle, the swinging note, the tiny hand-off note; 8 headline block (Geist lines, Caveat word, underline PNG with its ragged reveal) and the strike; 9 grain 0.03, static-seeded; NO vignette (it greys white paper and the paper recipe sets its own to 0 on purpose). Z exceptions: the question card at f784 sits above the code cards; in the team row the heads are in FRONT of the hero (they occlude his gloves and chin by design).

HERO TRANSFORMS (from the measured 1632 bounds; never from memory). ONE transform opens and closes the film so the loop is true: hang(132, 100, 816) -> bar y 308-392 (mid 350), bar x 205-874, head x 231-848, y 387-707, eyes (447, 479) and (630, 507), gloves y 351-433. Plan drop-in: hang(100, 92, 816) -> bar y 300-384, head x 199-816, y 379-699, eyes (415, 471) and (598, 499), right glove anchor (678, 384). 16:9: opening and end hang(70, -100, 979) -> bar y 150-251, head x 189-930, y 244-629, eyes (449, 355) and (667, 388); Plan hang(957, -135, 685). The hang() return (barTop, barMid, mid) positions the clay dot and the glove slaps.

LAUNCH REUSE. Up-and-over at f176: t_launch = (f - 176) * 1000/30 + 420 ms, unclamped: gather, pull (let-go f184/f186), spring, come-back f205/f207, pinch f215, suck f218, gone f227; he pops from the heap at f228. Plan exit at f508: the pull segment 560 -> 900 over f508-f518, a 4-frame short spring, then the come-back segment 1400 -> 2120 at 1.5x (gloves back f522/f523, pinch f529, suck f531, gone f536) via the new `from`/`speed` options. Return at f1032: new `drop` option (head dy -0.47*ART -> 0 with E.back(1.06), sway +4 -> 0 damped, squash 1.04, barDy mirrored); blink held 1 until f1056. Glove slaps f1016/f1020: draw each glove half from y -80 to 0 (E.o3, 4 f) with grip 0.12 for 3 f and the bar sagging 0.9 u. No holdAt, no barOffset: the bar is never left behind or lifted away; the only persistent bar is the painted one.

EASING FAMILIES. Entrances and landings: E.o3; travel and sweeps: E.io; pops: E.back(1.3-1.4) over 8-10 f; exits: E.i2/E.i3 over 5-8 f; presses: E.o5 over 4 f; 'late' slide: E.back(1.7) 6 f. Face swaps between peek PNGs are hard cuts: ALWAYS hide them inside a 2-frame 20 px dip behind the card edge. Blinks on the hang are 2 f of eyes sy 0.08 (keep the face layer); the sleeping slits are eyes sy 0.08 per eye about its own centre (eyes.each), never the blink layer, so the face reads as a face at frame 0. Breathing bob runs from frame 0 (period 64 f) and stops only at the comic hold (f144-f160) and the final stillness (f1164-).

PROCEDURAL VS PNG. PNG (pre-rendered by lift.mjs from components.jobs.mjs recipes, or existing), each in seeds A/B/C for the boil: paper (static, one seed), hero layers, peek faces (+ the nohands set and glove sprites), underlines (+ the regenerated moss one), dotted heads (static), mark-x0-ink, ring-ink-wide, hatch, tape (recoloured grey), listen-dots (recoloured Keybot clay), torn-note x6, strike-ink, brush-bar-stroke (pre-clipped by the bar's alpha), clay-dot, ink-sun, ink-dashes x2, ink-comma, ink-dot, ink-tick, beetle A/B, dip-pen frame/pills/stamp, tap-ring, sparkle-sea x2, pencil-ring. Procedural in the page: all cards and their type, the scrawl, the heap physics, eye tracking, the pendulum, the paper flips (scaleX about the centre line), stroke reveals (clip rects, diagonal clips, the conic clip for the 0, alpha-threshold ragged edges: draw the PNG into an offscreen, threshold its alpha at the current x, destination-in), ink specks, grain. Pre-render once per aspect: the paper crop. The ragged-edge reveal for underlines and the bar stroke: offscreen mask = the PNG's alpha where (x < edge + 34*fbm(y/40)); then destination-in on the layer. Brush PNGs are NEVER scaled non-uniformly (the only deliberate exception is underline()'s thick); hatch is drawn at one scale and clipped or tiled.

BUILD ORDER (critical path). Day one, before any beat: (1) peek-reach (nohands faces for curious/happy/shy/starry/hello in one renderArt run, so every ledge is measured, + glove sprites via the hands [] diff, + the raised glove) and decide its fallback within the hour; six gags depend on it. (2) hang() additions (grip, reach, drop, from/speed, eyes.each) and lid-L. (3) underline-4f7a3a regenerated; one MOSS constant #4F7A3A for the tick and the Yes fill; tape and listen-dots recolours. (4) The frame-grid timeline skeleton with every cut, so the sound cue list exists before the gags; render the sound through the 300 Hz high-pass proxy and fix the pulse/heart/boom bodies before any gag that depends on the beat is animated. (5) The three chrome overlays for --stills. Then the components recipes (seed A first, B/C for the boil last), then beats in order, rendering --range per beat.

TYPE SYSTEM. One headline system: Geist 900 left at x 72, two lines, no full stop, line pitch 1.15x; episode headlines 96 px (Caveat word 110 px) at baselines 370 and 480 (so line 2's descenders end near 510, 50 px above a peeking head top at ~560); the pile-up headline 120 px (Caveat 138) at baselines 1040/1178; the payoff 120 px at baselines 640/778; the Caveat word on the Geist baseline, its underline through underline() with wide 1.12 (1.3 for 'up', 'you', 'yes') and thick to >= 22 px tall, 8 px under the baseline. Readability floor: every real word >= 44 px at 1080 wide in Geist; handwriting bigger because Caveat's x-height is ~0.45 em (scrawl 68 px #5C5C5C, notes 52 px ink, 'yours'/'copy' 52 px); greys no lighter than #6B6B6B and only on Geist Mono code, 'Tests pass' and 'yours'; nothing is ever a bitmap crop of a screen; the code card has three lines at 44 px. Widest lines at 96 px: 'Nothing goes live' ~854 px (ends x 926), 'Your trip, sorted' ~800 px, both inside x 72-950.

SAFE AREAS (9:16). The safe box is y 270-1400 and x <= 950 below y 1000 (Reels' caption + audio row covers ~420-480 px at the bottom and its rail sits at x > 950 from y ~1000; TikTok covers ~550 px at the bottom; Shorts ~340; Meta's Reels ad spec reserves the top 14% and bottom 35%). Rules: all readable words, every pill, the Go live? card, the team names, the 'yours' slot and the Coming soon / x0bot.com stamp sit at y <= 1280, with the thesis and CTA lines at or above 1250; stage cards at x 72-940, y 850-1270 (day card to 1280); the hook card's text at y 1070-1200; the heap's visible tail below the stage cards (y 1270-1400) is the progress cue and is inside the box; the Plan bar at y 300 is under the 270 line; the end card's lowest ink is ~1280; the pile-up headline at baselines 1040/1178 is inside. --stills renders every checked frame under the Reels, Shorts and TikTok overlays. The poster frame for feeds is f36 (eyes open, the card dropping in behind his bar); for the store, f1168 (the end card). Never frame 0. Both are exported as separate cover PNGs.

ASPECTS AND CUT-DOWNS. v1 ships 9:16 (Reels, Shorts, TikTok) and 16:9 (the site, embeds, the Play feature graphic); 16:9 is NOT a pre-roll cut (the product is not named until f912), so if a skippable pre-roll is ever wanted it is a separate cut that opens on the end card's bar and mark. 4:5 and 1:1 are not crops of either master (the headline block and the stage card cannot both survive a crop); if needed they are a third composition later.
